text: Every umbrella at the stop pops open. Except Eli's. In this world, an umbrella only opens if someone is waiting for you to get home.
He shakes it. He bangs it. It stays shut. He checks his phone. No messages. He's lived alone since the spring.
So he walks home. Forty minutes. Soaked to the bone. Halfway home, it bursts open on its own.
In his front window, Pepper is waiting. Fourteen years old. He's been at the glass since six.
Hey, old man. You waited for me?
Eli doesn't buy a new umbrella. He doesn't need one.
